text:
Matt H: Quick question — we got a DSAR deletion for customer foo-corp. Which logs/traces do we need to fully erase vs pseudonymize? cc @privacy-team

Sarah L: Short answer: request_id traces and raw request bodies need deletion if they contain customer PII. App logs with customer_id must be redacted. We have retention exceptions — how old is the data?

Matt H: Most of it is within the last 90 days; a few traces ~400 days old are in the archived S3 bucket.

Lee: FYI, S3 lifecycle won't handle manual erase requests. We do one-off purge jobs for DSARs. Runbook here: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/purge-customer-data

Lee: Example command:
```
purge-customer-data --customer foo-corp --scope traces,request-logs --confirm
```

Anika: Which approvals do you have? We need legal sign-off + EngSec ack. Anything beyond retention window requires CISO approval per policy. @legal @eng-security :eyes: 

Matt H: Legal signed earlier today (email thread ID: LEG-2026-109). Can someone from infra run the job or grant me temporary permission?

ops-bot: Access request created: AR-9834 — awaiting infra-lead approval.

DevOps: I can run it if Lee/Infra is OK. Order of ops we use:
1) Tombstone customer ids in ES (don't delete immediately)
2) Run S3 purge for matching prefixes
3) Remove any debug snapshots and cache entries
4) Verify alerts and update ticket

Sarah L: Also make sure to run internal scrub for debug snapshots:
```
scripts/scrub_customer.py --id foo-corp --remove-raw-bodies
```

Matt H: Thanks all. Tagging @DevOps to pick up. I'll update ticket DSAR-548 with run details and post back once completed. :thumbsup:

DevOps: Roger. Will post the S3 purge job ID and confirmation when done.
